newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel GDP grew at 2.7 pct pace in fourth quarter.
newsitem.headline: Israel GDP grew at 2.7 pct pace in fourth quarter.

text.p: Israel's gross domestic product grew at an annualised rate of 2.7 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996, the same rate as the previous quarter, the Central Bureau of Statistics said on Wednesday.
"A look at the components of GDP shows a drop in per capita private consumption concentrated in durable goods and a reduction in investment in fixed assets," the bureau said.
In the year-earlier quarter, GDP rose at a 1.8 percent annualised rate.
The bureau did not provide a full-year figure for GDP growth, although in December it gave a preliminary estimate of 4.4 percent, down from 7.1 percent in 1996.
In the second half, GDP rose at a 3.0 percent rate, compared with 4.1 percent in the first half. Israel's economic growth has been slowing since the first quarter of last year.

Private consumption rose at a 1.8 percent rate in the fourth quarter, slowing from a 7.5 percent rate in the third quarter and 8.6 percent rate a year ago, the bureau said. Per capita consumption dropped at a 1.2 percent rate, following a third-quarter 4.7 percent increase.
Consumption of durable goods plunged at a 38.2 percent pace in the fourth rate quarter following rises of 17.7 percent in the third quarter and 44 percent a year earlier.
The bureau said investment in fixed assets dropped at a 14.1 percent rate in the quarter, following an increase of 21.2 percent in the third quarter and 13.4 percent a year ago.

Investment in residential construction rose at a 10.4 percent annualised rate following increases at rates of 2.2 percent in the third quarter and 7.8 percent a year earlier. Investment in other sectors dropped at a 23.3 percent pace following increases of 30.9 percent in the third quarter and 15.9 percent a year earlier.
Exports of goods and services declined at a 0.6 percent rate in the fourth quarter compared with a 19.4 percent rate third-quarter increase and an 8.2 percent rise a year ago, the bureau said.
Imports of goods and services dropped at a 14.6 percent rate compared with a 25.6 percent increase in the third quarter and a 38.3 percent increase a year ago.
